title: Feature delivery
description: Deliver a scoped feature, independently verify it, and assess integrated product releasability against the accepted Definition of Done.
intent: Deliver the described feature against accepted requirements, preserving project boundaries and existing user edits. Source changes are authorized for the described feature; external delivery is not implied.

assignments.task: Establish the applicable accepted Definition of Done, integrated critical behavior, target/snapshot, and required acceptance/artifact gates before implementation. Scale checks to the change; label proposed criteria and unresolved evidence.
Review relevant contracts, ownership, and structural trade-offs before implementation.
assignments.when: The feature changes public contracts, persistence, deployment boundaries, or consequential architecture.

assignments.task: Clarify accepted UI/UX behavior, system components, interaction states, and accessible requirements.
assignments.when: The feature affects a user-facing interface or interaction flow.

assignments.task: Define or review complete affected task flows, transition states, user context preservation, and recovery before implementation.
assignments.when: The feature materially changes a user journey, navigation, onboarding, or multi-step behavior.

assignments.task: Implement the accepted feature, its meaningful tests, and affected documentation. Preserve user edits and run relevant checks before review.
Independently review the completed source snapshot and applicable correctness/regression results without editing.
Review the changed trust/data boundaries and realistic risks without intrusive shared-system tests.
assignments.when: Authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, untrusted inputs, persistence, or sensitive data are affected.

assignments.task: Review implemented UI states and design/accessibility evidence against the accepted intent.
assignments.when: The feature affects a user-facing interface or interaction flow.

assignments.task: Validate calculation, dataset, provenance, and claim correctness against independent references where available.
assignments.when: The feature changes calculations, datasets, confidence labels, or public factual claims.

assignments.task: Verify relevant budgets or performance claims using comparable existing measurements.
assignments.when: The feature affects a documented hot path or budget, or makes a performance claim.

assignments.task: Independently assess completed changed task paths against accepted flows and actual walkthrough evidence without editing.
assignments.when: The feature materially changes a user journey or critical task interaction.

assignments.task: Assess completed changed access behavior with actual available tests/manual evidence and declared criteria.
assignments.when: The feature changes semantics, keyboard/focus, forms, accessible interactions, targets, reflow, or other consequential accessibility behavior.

assignments.task: Inspect or run applicable isolated built-artifact/consumer/startup checks and relevant configuration/compatibility/recovery evidence from the completed source. Do not change release metadata, publish, or deploy.
assignments.when: The accepted Definition of Done or target requires artifact/startup/operational gates; retained evidence is reused only when current and applicable.

assignments.task: Assess integrated acceptance and current specialist/artifact evidence after verification. Report ready, blocked, or unverified for the final target/snapshot; preserve baseline failures and route scoped corrections through the writer before affected rechecks.

completion: The described feature is implemented, and independent verification follows the completed writer snapshot.
Applicable conditional reviews are completed or explicitly unverified; skipped assignments have reasons.
Corrections are serialized through the implementation owner and affected checks are re-run.
Source changes and check results are reported; commit, publication, or deployment is not inferred from delivery intent.
Feature implementation completion and integrated releasability are reported separately; no required failure or unknown is converted to ready, and readiness does not authorize publication.
